charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Carrefour SA: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Carrefour SA: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Carrefour SA: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Carrefour SA: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Carrefour SA: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Carrefour SA: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

recurringOperatingIncome.title: Recurring operating income
recurringOperatingIncome.content:
Recurring operating income is Carrefour's own non-GAAP profitability measure: operating income excluding non-recurring items (restructuring, impairments, disposal gains/losses, and other one-offs management flags out). It is the margin figure Carrefour and sell-side analysts quote in results commentary and guidance, not statutory operating income.

For Carrefour SA: recurring operating income has been roughly flat to slightly declining since FY2022 (€2,377m) through FY2025 (€2,158m) despite revenue growth, so the margin line (right axis) is the more informative read than the absolute level -- it has drifted down from the mid-2% area, consistent with French food-retail price competition and cost inflation squeezing the recurring margin even as top-line sales (ex-VAT) held up.

What to watch:

  • Recurring operating margin trend versus statutory operating margin -- a widening gap means one-offs are doing more of the work
  • H1 is seasonally the weaker half for French grocers; compare H1-to-H1 and FY-to-FY, not H1 to FY
  • Guidance is typically given in recurring operating income terms, so this is the number to check against management's targets

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Carrefour SA: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Carrefour SA: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Carrefour SA: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: 2026-10-26, one pass per Step 8c.5. Trip: implied P/E 56.9x on base IV 24.96 vs 2x 10yr avg 15.5x; P/B 1.56x and P/Sales 0.204x were also above the decade maxima (1.31x, 0.180x). Not a peak-earnings case (item 1 skipped: owner-FCF base already normalised below actual and below guidance). Applied item 2: WACC 7.5% -> 9.0% with explicit premiums (+0.5% LatAm geographic/currency, +0.5% French regulatory/political, +0.5% thin-margin cyclicality), documented in inputs.wacc_rationale. Applied item 3: base revenue growth capped at the through-cycle CAGR (FY2016-FY2025 = 0.717%, applied at 0.7%) from year 2, bull trimmed to 2.0% continuing LFL, bear 0-0.5%; selected_growth_rate 2.0 -> 0.7. Second (final) adjustment after the first pass still tripped: capped years trimmed 0.72 -> 0.70 so the growth_too_high candidate clears exactly; a further WACC increase was NOT taken because passing the P/E rule would require a base value below the share price. Applied item 4: terminal caps reset to the decade's observed owner-FCF multiple range, bear 8x / base 10x / bull 12x (EV/EBITDA history null; engine prints implied terminal EV/EBITDA for cross-check). Unchanged: margin/D&A/capex/tax paths, 30/50/20 weights, EUR 1,900m seasonal WC add-back (re-examined, retained as a timing-consistency item). The P/E rule divides by trough FY2025 SBC-adjusted EPS (~EUR 0.44; 71% ETR, Italy disposal loss) and is already at 31.5x on the current share price, so it cannot be passed by any value above the market price; it is reported as still tripped rather than engineered around.
